THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE H.T. NARENDRA PRASAD  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

These appeals under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') have been filed by the claimants challenging by the judgment dated 05.10.2015 passed by MACT, Bengaluru in MVC No.2923/2014 and MVC No.2924/2014 respectively.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals briefly stated are that on 10.06.2014 when the claimants along with others were traveling in car bearing registration No.KA-01-MA-624 near Karekallu Cross, Bengaluru being driven by claimant in MVC 2923/2014, at that time, the driver of LGV bearing registration No.KA-42-A-865 being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and NC: 2024:KHC:37824 MFA No. 5267 of 2018 C/W negligent manner, dashed to the car.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimants sustained grievous injuries and were hospitalized.
3. The claimants filed petitions under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that they spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondents appeared through counsel and filed written statements denying the averments made in the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the claim petitions and held that NC: 2024:KHC:37824 MFA No. 5267 of 2018 C/W the accident occurred due to contributory negligence of drivers of both the vehicles at 80% negligence on the part of the driver of the goods vehicle and 20% on the part of the driver of the car.

Further, the Tribunal held that after deducting 20% negligence, the claimant in MVC 2923/2024 is entitled to a compensation of Rs.465,600/- and claimant in MVC 2924/2014 is entitled to a compensation of Rs.406,400/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeals have been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following contentions:

3 NEGLIGENCE:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The accident occurred due to sole negligence of the part of the driver of the goods vehicle.
Immediately after the accident, complaint has been lodged and FIR has been registered against the driver of the goods vehicle.
The police after thorough investigation have filed charge sheet NC: 2024:KHC:37824 MFA No. 5267 of 2018 C/W against the driver of the goods vehicle.

The Tribunal only on the basis of the panchanama, which is drawn after 4 days of the accident, has come to the conclusion that the driver of the car has contributed to the accident to the extent of 20%.
The said finding of the Tribunal is contrary to the materials available on record.
PWs-1 and 2 have categorically stated that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the goods vehicle by its driver.
To disprove the case, the respondent-Insurance Company has not examined any witness.
QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION
Considering the evidences of the claimant and doctor, nature of injuries and medical records, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal in both the cases is inadequate.
With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeals.
On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter- contentions:

NEGLIGENCE It is not in dispute that the accident took place on the middle of the road and it is also admitted by PWs-1 and 2 that the driver of the car had seen the goods vehicle coming from the opposite direction at a distance of 60 feet.
Inspite of that, the driver of the car was proceeding in the middle of the road at a high speed and in rash and negligent manner.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly held that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of driver of the car as well as the driver of the goods vehicle.
Even as per the panchanama and IMV report, the driver of the car has also contributed to the accident.
Hence, the Tribunal has rightly held that the driver of the car has also contributed to the accident to the extent of 20%.
There is no error in the said finding of the Tribunal.
N C : 2 0 2 4 : K H C : 3 7 8 2 4 M F A N o . 5 2 6 7 o f 2 0 1 8 C / W Q U A N T U M O F COMPENSATION:

Considering the age and avocation of the claimants, injuries sustained by the claimants the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal in both the cases is just and reasonable and it does not warrant interference.

However, in light of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others -v- Venkateshan.V and others (MFA 5896/2018 and connected matters disposed of on Chajjaram vs Naveen R on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94144009/
4 24.8.2020), the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% p.a. on the compensation amount appears excessive.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
NEGLIGENCE:
9.

The specific case of the claimants is that on 10.06.2014 when the claimants along with others were NC: 2024:KHC:37824 MFA No. 5267 of 2018 C/W traveling in car bearing registration No.KA-01-MA-624 near Karekallu Cross, Bengaluru driven by claimant in MVC 2923/2014, at that time, the driver of LGV bearing registration No.KA-42-A-865 being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the car.

As a result of the aforesaid accident,
the claimants sustained grievous injuries and were hospitalized.

After recovering from the injuries,
the claimants have filed the claim petitions.
10. To prove the case, the claimants have examined themselves as PWs-1 and 2 and produced 40 documents.
The claimants in their evidences have reiterated the averments made in the claim petitions.
11. Under the Motor Vehicles Act in the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in the civil case.

No doubt,
before the Tribunal, there must be some material on the basis of which the Tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to decide for awarding - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:37824 MFA No. 5267 of 2018 C/W compensation, but the Tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt a nicety of a civil or criminal case.
After all it is a summary enquiry and it is the legislation for the welfare of the Society.
The proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings under civil rules.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

In the case of MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (2018) 5 SCC 656, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as hereinbelow:
"25.

sentences.text: In Dulcina Fernandes, this Court examined similar situation where the evidence of claimant's eyewitness was discarded by the Tribunal and that the respondent in that case was acquitted in the criminal case concerning the accident.

This Court,
however, opined that it cannot be overlooked that upon investigation of the case registered against the respondent, prima facie, materials showing negligence were found to put him on trial.

The Court restated the settled principle that the evidence of the claimants ought to be examined by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly the standard of proof - 11 - Chajjaram vs Naveen R on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94144009/
5 NC: 2024:KHC:37824 MFA No. 5267 of 2018 C/W beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
12.
The claimants have stated that due to the accidental injuries, they could not lodge the complaint immediately and only on 15.06.2014, they have lodged the complaint.
The police have registered FIR and after thorough investigation, they have filed charge sheet against the driver of the goods vehicle.
The police have drawn panchanama as per Ex.P-2 and MVA report as per Ex.P-3.
It is very clear from panchanama and MVA report that accident occurred on the middle of the road and front portion of both the vehicles have been fully damaged.
In the evidence of PWs-1 and 2, it is admitted that accident occurred on the straight road and the driver of the car was able to see the goods vehicle coming at the distance of 60 feet.

It is very clear that the accident occurred on straight middle road and if the drivers of the both the vehicles were little cautious, they could have controlled and avoided the occurrence of accident.

Therefore, taking into consideration the evidence of parties and materials available on record such as FIR, complaint, panchanama, MVA report and charge sheet, this Court is of the opinion that the drivers of both the vehicles have contributed to the accident.
It is held that the driver of goods vehicle has contributed to the accident to the extent of 80% and driver of the car has contributed to the accident to the extent of 20%.
There is no error in the said finding of the Tribunal.
Hence, the finding of the Tribunal regarding negligence, is confirmed.

QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:
IN MFA 5267/2018 (MVC 2923/2014)
13.

The Tribunal, considering the age and avocation of the claimant has rightly assessed the income of the claimant at Rs.9,000/- p.m. and considering the evidence of the doctor has rightly taken the whole body disability at 10%.
Further, by applying the correct multiplier of '16' has rightly awarded compensation of Rs.173,000/- under the head of 'loss of future income'.
The nature of injuries indicates that the claimant must have been under rest and treatment for a period of 4 months.

Consequently, the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.36,000/-
(Rs.9,000*4 months) under the head 'loss of income during laid up period'.
15.
The claimant was hospitalized as an inpatient for more than 7 days in the hospital and subsequently received further treatment.

Therefore, I am inclined to enhance the compensation awarded under the head of 'food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges' from Rs.10,000/- to Rs.20,000/-.

Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injuries and also undergone surgery.

Considering the prolonged pain during treatment as well as the permanent disability certified by the doctor, I am inclined to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'pain and sufferings' from Rs.60,000/-
- 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:37824 MFA No. 5267 of 2018 C/W to Rs.75,000/- and

under the head of 'loss of amenities' from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.50,000/-.
17. Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.
